description: Searching knowledge: the rules a kb_search answer follows, never how it is ranked. 'check-' cases give the session's 'overlays' (as knowledge.json), the call's 'arguments', the declared 'modes', optional 'limits' and an answer 'response'; expect the sorted ids of the rules it breaks ('overlays', 'mode', 'top', 'path-limit', 'not-knowledge', 'range', 'text', 'inert', 'order', 'shape'), none when it conforms. 'order-' cases give 'passages' and expect their order by the answer's ordering rule.

cases.description: One overlay, one passage: the shape is the whole contract.
An overlay with nothing to say gives an empty list, not an error.
A note is allowed on an entry.

results.note: embeddings are not available; matched by words

cases.description: A note is served text: a control character in it is written out.
An overlay that cannot answer says so in its entry, and the call does not fail.

error.message: the index is still being made

cases.description: An entry's error is one of two classes.
A mode asked for by name and not available for an overlay.
'auto' is never unavailable: the server answers with a mode it has.
An entry holds passages or an error, never both.
One entry per overlay in the order the session has them.
An entry is missing.
Entries out of order.
With 'overlay', only that overlay answers.
An entry for an overlay the call excluded.
A named mode is the one that answers.
A named mode is never answered by another.
'auto' may be answered by any declared mode, and the entry says which.
A mode the server does not declare.
More passages than 'top'.
'top' counts per overlay, not over the whole call.
Absent, 'top' is 5.
Highest score first.
Equal scores: path bytes.
Equal scores, in path order.
Equal scores and path: first line.
Equal in all but the last line: the shorter first.
A score may be negative; order is still highest first.
A score is a number.
A boolean is no number.
An integer score is a number.
'path' limits to a file, or the files under a folder.
A path naming a file.
A passage outside the limit.
'kb' is a folder, not a prefix of a name: 'kb/intro.md' is not under 'kb/int'.
And a folder 'kb' does not hold 'kbx/a'.
A passage of a file the overlay does not serve.
A file that names markdown is served without that line, so its first line is the next one.
The shebang line is not in the text a passage lies in.
A passage is of the text kb_read serves with no context, ${...} replaced: here the name of the overlay.
The stored text, with its placeholders, is not what is served.
An included file's text is in its includer's lines: lines 2 and 3 of lc.md are the first two of multi.md.
Line 4 of the stored lc.md is past its end; of the served text it is the last of the include.
A file whose includes cycle cannot be served and is no passage's file.
A raw file is served from its second line, so its first served line is the third of the stored file.
A file that is not markdown is searched as it is stored: its first line is its first line.
And nothing in it is replaced.
A file for an engine this server lacks is served with its first line and a context block, and a passage lies in that text.
A file for an engine this server renders is searched as it is served, with no context: the first line of env.md is the overlay name and root.
On a server without envsubst the same file is served as written with its first line and a context block: a passage of the rendered text is not in it.
The first line is 1.
The last line is not before the first.
A line past the file's last.
The last line is inclusive: line 6 alone.
The text lies in its lines.
A line that is long may be cut: the text is part of it.
A text that is not in its lines.
A passage has text.
CR is no part of the lines the text is checked against.
Passage text is served as kb_read serves it: controls written out.
Raw, an escape character in a passage.
A heading is written out too.
A heading may be empty.
A passage has these keys and no other.
And all of them.
An entry has overlay, mode, passages and perhaps a note.
The answer is {"results"} alone.
The answer is an object.
'results' is a list.
Highest score first.
Equal scores: path, compared as bytes.
Bytes, not UTF-16 units: U+FB01 (EF AC 81) comes before U+1F600 (F0 9F 98 80), though UTF-16 puts U+1F600 first.
Equal score and path: first line, then last line.
Scores below zero.
Passages equal in every key keep the order given.
An integer and a float of one value are equal.
